title: 1926 Wolvertem Fokker F.VII crash
summary: KLM Fokker F.VII encountered dense fog while on scheduled Amsterdam-Brussels-Paris service. The pilot attempted to maintain visual contact with the ground by descending to approximately 50 meters altitude. Unable to avoid terrain at low altitude, the aircraft struck trees and crashed near Wolvertem, Belgium, killing both occupants.
probable_cause: Controlled flight into terrain due to dense fog and loss of situational awareness. The pilot descended to low altitude to maintain visual reference but was unable to avoid terrain. The localized nature of the fog and lack of prior weather forecasting contributed to the accident.

factors.evidence: aircraft encountered unexpectedly dense and localized fog
pilot circled the area for approximately 20 minutes searching for clearer conditions, unable to maintain orientation in the poor visibility
pilot descended to a low altitude, estimated at around 50 meters, to regain visual contact with the ground
aircraft struck the ground in a wooded area while flying at low altitude, made three large bounces, then exploded

events.text: Departed Waalhaven Airport in Rotterdam at 09:03 local time
Encountered dense and localized fog near Wolvertem, approximately 15 km northwest of Brussels
Pilot descended to approximately 50 meters altitude to regain visual contact with the ground
Aircraft struck wooded area and crashed in wheat field, made three large bounces then exploded, both occupants killed instantly

title: 1926 Paris–Bucharest Potez 25 crash
summary: A Potez 25 aircraft struck mountainous terrain in the Jeseníky Mountains of Czechoslovakia during a planned non-stop flight from Paris to Bucharest. After encountering dense fog, the crew deviated northeast from their intended route in an attempt to regain the direct route and struck the main ridge of the mountains. Pilot Gheorghe Bănciulescu survived with severe injuries requiring amputation of both legs while pilot-mechanic Ioan Stoica died during evacuation from the crash site.

factors.evidence: crew deviated north-east from their intended route and struck the main ridge of the Jeseníky Mountains
Bănciulescu's attempt to avoid the fog was influenced by a dangerous encounter with similar conditions in the same mountainous region during the outward flight
struck the main ridge of the Jeseníky Mountains near Jelení studánka

events.text: The aircraft was on a long-distance flight from Paris to Bucharest, having completed more than half of the journey in favourable conditions.
After encountering dense fog, the crew decided to enter the fog in an attempt to regain the direct route near Vienna.
The aircraft's left wing struck the ridge, causing the aircraft to turn violently and break apart near Jelení studánka.
Pilot-mechanic Ioan Stoica died during evacuation from the crash site.

notes: exceptional historical record with detailed investigation
crew action influenced by previous encounter with same hazard

title: Leigh air disaster
summary: A Blériot 155 aircraft operating a Paris to Croydon service encountered a fire in the port upper engine at 3:27 pm GMT while cruising. The fire spread to the wing and the aircraft changed direction toward Penshurst Airfield. The tail sank while the aircraft gained brief height, then rolled over and dived to the ground where it burned. This was the first recorded in-flight fire on an airliner.
probable_cause: In-flight fire in port upper engine that spread to the wing, causing loss of control.

factors.evidence: the port upper engine on fire and the fire was seen to spread to the wing
Then the aircraft rolled over and dived to the ground
the wreckage was consumed by fire and a petrol tank exploded

events.text: The aircraft departed Le Bourget Airport, Paris at 1:30 pm local time (12:30 pm GMT) bound for Croydon Airport.
At 3:24 pm GMT, the pilot radioed ahead to Croydon OK, passing over Tonbridge. All well.
At 3:27 pm, eyewitnesses reported seeing the aircraft with the port upper engine on fire; the fire was seen to spread to the wing.
Then the aircraft rolled over and dived to the ground where the wreckage was consumed by fire in the grounds of Southwood, Leigh, Kent.
